chunks: That was narrated - Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Ali ibn Hanthalah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who married his own umm al-walad (concubine mother of his child) from among his slaves, and then the slave was manumitted after he had consummated the marriage with her; does she have the choice [to annul or keep]? He said, 'No. She married him while he was a slave and accepted him as such, so when he became free, she is more entitled to accept him [as her husband].'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-walad: A female slave who bears a child to her master, gaining specific legal status
key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: Al-khiyar: The right of choice or option to annul or confirm a contract

ai.seo_question: Does a concubine have the right to annul her marriage if her master's slave husband is freed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that an *umm al-walad* married to a slave retains her marital bond upon his manumission, as she consented to the union while he was a slave and thus has no right to annul it based on his elevated status. This ruling underscores the principle of *rida* (consent) in Islamic jurisprudence, emphasizing that the initial validity of the contract remains intact despite the change in the husband's social standing. It highlights the flexibility of marital contracts in Shia fiqh, where the status of the parties at the time of marriage is decisive for continuity.
